description:
Search the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED database for economic
        data series by keyword. Returns series ID, title, frequency, units,
        seasonal adjustment, and date range.

        Use this tool when:
        - You need to find the right FRED series ID before fetching data
        - You want to discover what macro data is available for a topic
        - You are looking for interest rates, inflation, GDP, unemployment, or
          money supply series to provide macro context for financial analysis

        Common series IDs (use GetFredSeriesData after finding one):
        - DGS10: 10-Year Treasury Yield
        - CPIAUCSL: Consumer Price Index (CPI-U)
        - UNRATE: Unemployment Rate
        - GDP: Gross Domestic Product
        - FEDFUNDS: Federal Funds Rate
        - M2SL: M2 Money Supply

        Requires FRED_API_KEY environment variable (free at fred.stlouisfed.org).
        Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED API.

FredSeriesSearchParams.description: Search FRED for economic data series by keyword.

additional_display_fields.description: List of additional fields to display (e.g. ['firm_name', 'rep_name'])
additional_display_fields.title: Additional Display Fields

limit.description: Maximum number of series to return. Default 20, max 1000.
limit.title: Limit

mcp_prompt_id.description: Unique prompt ID for the MCP session. This can be used for tracking and logging purposes. Do not change this value.
mcp_prompt_id.title: Mcp Prompt Id

optional_additional_filters.description: Dictionary of additional filters not covered by other fields
optional_additional_filters.title: Optional Additional Filters

order_by.description: Sort order. Options: 'search_rank' (default, most relevant first), 'popularity' (most used), 'last_updated'.
order_by.title: Order By

query.description: Keywords to search for economic series. Examples: '10-year treasury', 'CPI', 'unemployment rate', 'GDP', 'federal funds rate'.
query.title: Query

question_asked.description: Question asked by the user. Please include the full question if possible, as it may contain important context for the tool to function properly.
question_asked.title: Question Asked

source_resource_id.description:
Optional resource_id of a previously cached result set (returned by a prior Fetch tool call).
        When provided, the tool will load the full dataset directly from the cache folder instead of
        re-executing the query against the database. Pass this when the user is asking a follow-up
        question or a different grouping/filter on data that was already fetched. 
        Also, use this, when one tool output is an input for another tool.
source_resource_id.title: Source Resource Id

wholesaler_ids.description:
List of wholesaler IDs or names to filter results by the internal fin user
        who owns or manages the data. If names are provided instead of IDs, the system will automatically
        resolve them to their corresponding USER_IDs before applying the filter.
        
        In fin, users are assigned one of three roles:
        - Wholesaler: A field-level sales representative responsible for a specific territory, channel,
        or book of accounts. This is the most granular user type. Most sales data, advisor relationships,
        and touchpoints in fin are owned at the wholesaler level.
        - Manager: Oversees a team of Wholesalers, typically organized by territory or sales channel
        (e.g., Regional Manager, Channel Manager). Filtering by a Manager ID will scope results
        to that Manager's purview across their team.
        - Executive: C-suite level users (e.g., CEO, CFO, COO) at the asset manager / fund company
        level (e.g., PIMCO, MetLife, BlackRock). Executives have the broadest visibility and their
        ID represents an org-wide scope.

        Accepts either:
        - User IDs directly (e.g., ['WS001', 'MGR045'])
        - Full or partial user names (e.g., ['John Smith', 'Sarah']) — these will be resolved to IDs
        - A mix of both (e.g., ['WS001', 'Sarah Connor'])

        If omitted, data is returned based on the authenticated user's role and their default data scope.
        Examples: ['WS001'], ['WS001', 'MGR045'], ['John Smith'], ['John Smith', 'WS002']
wholesaler_ids.title: Wholesaler Ids
